Oliver was now 8th and Rutland 9th, Bob Readman, seemingly taking it easy, 10th, and Tony Bellchamber, also walking his first 20 very strongly, 11th.
At the start, Allen got away very fast with Bert Clayton close on his heels and the rest of our boys well up filling various positions from George Oliver 15 to Tony Bellchamber 60.
Tony Bellchamber finished 2nd in the Inter-Banks 7 Miles Road Walking Championship. Len Herbert ran very well to finish 2nd in the Inter-Counties 3 miles run when he clocked 14 mins. 37.8 secs.
Tony Bellchamber completed the “A” team, and he would no doubt have been further up had he not had trouble with his tummy, which caused him to dart into the hedgerows from time to time.
In the absence of our leading scratch men, Tony Bellchamber carried the Club colours with great credit and in finishing 17th out of 149 starters, was our first man home.
The team were informed quickly, but worse was to follow when Tony Bellchamber was pulled at 5½ miles. Then the whips came out and the lads were pushed on.
While Hugh McGreechan was scoring 4th, our next positions were Harry Shields 28th, George Checkley 37th, Jack Wakeley 38th, Tony Bellchamber 41st, and Fred Rolfe 42nd.
